The internal annotation refers to retired reward.toml/pinned-judge wording; applied the authoritative staged sheet and frozen skill instead. Frozen references/quality-checks.md:104-106 requires complete scoring/all five judge files, the browser in every dimension, functional-only restart wiring, typed positive-weight unique criteria and resolving prompts.

All paths below beginning task/ are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/. Read and parsed all five judge.toml files and task.toml with Python 3.12 tomllib. task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 contains exactly gates render=0.0 and constraints=0.0, weights functional=0.6/polish=0.2/visual=0.2, and floor functional=0.05. Every key maps to its correctly named gates/ or scored/ directory; no listed dimension is missing. It is byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml.

Each task/tests/gates/{render,constraints}/judge.toml:1-15 and task/tests/scored/{polish,visual}/judge.toml:1-15 has judge='claude-code', mode='batched', an integer positive timeout, boolean isolated=false, prompt_template='prompt.md', and a stdio playwright-mcp with the configured Chromium executable. Functional has the same browser at task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:1-12 and alone adds name='verifier', command='/usr/local/bin/python3', args=['/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py', '$APP_RESTART_HELPER'] at lines 14-18. No judge block contains model, reasoning_effort, temperature or weight. Fallback matches task.toml's REWARDKIT_JUDGE. Both gates aggregate all_pass; all scored dimensions aggregate weighted_mean.

Checked every criterion, not a sample: render 1 binary, constraints 1 binary, functional 64 binary, polish 7 binary, visual 6 likert with points=5. All 79 IDs are globally unique as well as unique per file; names/descriptions are nonempty; weights are finite positive numbers. Per-file criterion weight totals are respectively 1, 1, 32.7, 4 and 6. These are relative weighted-mean inputs, so only scoring.toml dimension weights must sum to one. All six visual criteria supply the five integer anchors (visual/judge.toml:17-105).

Every prompt_template resolves to its neighboring actual prompt.md. Each of the five files contains both placeholders; in-memory execution of the same app-context replacement leaves no {app_context} and preserves {criteria} for RewardKit: render/prompt.md:12,22; constraints/prompt.md:13,35; functional/prompt.md:3,460; polish/prompt.md:11,51; visual/prompt.md:11,53. app_context.md exists, is nonempty, and has Application, Accounts and Key screens. test.sh:195-201 performs this replacement before suite invocation. task/tests/tools/score.py:10 resolves its actual ../scoring.toml location.

Restart is structurally connected: test.sh:127-190 generates the helper and substitutes its runtime paths, :191 makes it executable, :192 resets the single-use marker, and :193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER before either suite. The literal dollar-variable argument is intentional under the frozen staged-task-contract.md section 'tests/<suite>/<dimension>/judge.toml'; it is not an unresolved task placeholder. restart_mcp.py:9 consumes argv[1], :14 names restart_app, :25-47 invokes that helper, and :75-80 handles the tool call. Functional/prompt.md:23 and :410,415 call restart_app exactly once for the shared S22 scenario; other dimensions have no verifier server. tests/Dockerfile:19,31,33-38,43-45 supplies Playwright MCP, pinned RewardKit, Chromium and /tests. No image or MCP runtime was launched in this review.

Source assertions verified gates run before scored, score.py follows each suite (test.sh:213-227), and exports/substitution precede both. Configured timeout sums satisfy 600+600=1200<1500; 9000+900+900=10800<11100; 1500+11100=12600<task.toml verifier timeout 13200. These are configuration measurements, not evidence of actual judge completion time.

Adversarial structural checks: an in-memory conforming positive relative criterion weight change was accepted without requiring per-file normalization. In-memory broken copies with missing Playwright, duplicate criterion ID, zero criterion weight, or forbidden judge-level dimension weight were each rejected by the manual assertions. No task files changed. At the product level, a conforming UI with native/composite controls or a different layout is not structurally excluded: functional/prompt.md:11 explicitly locates controls by purpose; polish/prompt.md:43-47 permits composite controls.

Boundary of this Pass: test.sh, score.py and restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to the frozen template, but canonical identity does not establish behavioral correctness. I independently verified the raw-evidence-index hash of inherited-restart-counterexample.json, its test.sh SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, and its embedded-helper SHA256 0db23e8c7c8d70c7e934c4d13ccbb2326a4da2cb47f1b2ba1967009d829be3b7 against the frozen source; also read its reproduction script. That existing raw observation shows helper_returncode=0, old_still_running=true, before/after PID 7, claimed new PID 67, and EADDRINUSE. test.sh:152-183 explains it: the helper proceeds after its TERM wait and accepts HTTP availability without proving old termination/new-process liveness. This is an inherited runtime restart-helper defect, not a missing or mismatched structural wire; it requires separate runtime/durability adjudication and this structural Pass does not refute it. No new Docker run was made. Full configured judge, Oracle, target-model performance and judge workload remain unmeasured, as stated by the raw evidence index. This review does not clear those checks or the whole task.
